s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of systemic illness with multi-organ involvement, characterized by weakness, depression, drowsiness, and altered mental status, with laboratory evidence of metabolic derangements and imaging findings suggestive of lymphoproliferative disorder
salient_findings: Prolonged weakness, depression, and drowsiness
Elevated blood calcium and phosphorus levels
Abnormal blood gas with high lactate levels
Splenomegaly with increased glucose metabolism on PET/CT
Abnormal bone marrow aspiration with 24.6% abnormal cells
key_facts: Patient has a 16-year history of type II diabetes mellitus
Patient's diabetes was well-controlled with dagliflozin and metformin
Patient experienced weakness, depression, and drowsiness for more than 4 months
Patient was admitted to EICU due to faint consciousness and drowsiness
Initial vital signs showed rapid heart rate, shortness of breath, and fever
Blood calcium level was 4.86 mmol/L, which is above the normal range
Parathyroid hormone level was 8.27 pg/ml, which is below the normal range
Blood gas showed a pH of 7.32 and lactate level of 15 mmol/L
White blood cell count was elevated at 37.81 × 10^9/L
Hemoglobin level was low at 91 g/L
Lactate dehydrogenase level was elevated at 4285 mmol/L
PET/CT findings showed splenomegaly and diffuse increased glucose metabolism in liver and lymph nodes
Bone marrow aspiration showed 24.6% abnormal cells with specific immunophenotypic markers

shortlist.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: elevated lactate dehydrogenase and systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly with increased glucose metabolism

shortlist.label: T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: abnormal cells in bone marrow with specific immunophenotypic markers

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of weakness, depression, and drowsiness, along with laboratory findings of elevated lactate dehydrogenase, hypercalcemia, and low parathyroid hormone, is consistent with Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma. The PET/CT findings of splenomegaly and diffuse increased glucose metabolism in liver and lymph nodes, as well as the bone marrow aspiration showing abnormal cells with specific immunophenotypic markers, further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's immunophenotypic markers, such as CD2, CD5, and CD79α, do not support a diagnosis of Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which typically expresses CD20.

rejected.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: While Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a broad category, the specific findings in this case, such as the presence of CD4, CD38, and ckappa positive cells, are more consistent with Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.

rejected.label: T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and laboratory findings do not support a diagnosis of T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia, which typically presents with a high white blood cell count and specific immunophenotypic markers.

rejected.label: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's immunophenotypic markers and laboratory findings do not support a diagnosis of Anaplastic large cell lymphoma, which typically expresses CD30 and has distinct morphological features.
